subject: Proposed carveouts: feedback & usage paths
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudwave.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Doyle <mdoyle@cloudwave.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: CloudWave MSA: redlines around output ownership & training use

Ben — attaching our marked MSA. High level asks: 
- CloudWave retains title to all customer outputs and artifacts produced by the service. No assignment to vendor.
- No model training/fine-tuning on CloudWave data; any use of customer data for model improvement must be explicit opt-in and limited to anonymized telemetry.
- Feedback license must be narrowly scoped: limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, solely for improving Redwood’s service for CloudWave, with options for opt-out.
- Retention limits for logs and a clear deletion process on contract termination.

We flagged specific redlines in the attached CloudWave_MSA_redline_v3.docx and included a short summary (redline_summary.pdf). Procurement would like proposed language from Redwood legal to review before the next commercial call. Can you loop in legal?

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Director, Procurement — CloudWave
Attachments: CloudWave_MSA_redline_v3.docx (document), redline_summary.pdf (summary)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Michael Doyle <mdoyle@cloudwave.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CloudWave MSA: redlines around output ownership & training use

Lena — thanks for the clear redlines and the summary. I’ve looped in our legal (Kimberly) and SE (Evelyn) so we can propose clean contract language.

Quick summary of our position and a proposed middle ground to move the deal:
- Customer outputs: we can accept explicit ownership for customer-generated outputs and deliverables. We’ll propose language that reserves for CloudWave ownership while allowing Redwood to use non-identifiable telemetry for debugging and performance monitoring.
- Training/use of customer data: we cannot train public-facing foundational models on identifiable customer data by default. Proposed compromise: no model training/fine-tuning on CloudWave production data without explicit, documented opt-in; however, Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry (e.g., token counts, latency, anonymized error traces) to improve the service.
- Feedback license: propose a narrow, revocable license for anonymized feedback for the sole purpose of service improvement; transferable or sublicensable uses will be blocked.

I attached a short response draft (redline_response_v1.docx) so legal can review. Proposed next steps: Kimberly, can you prepare clause text we can send back this week? Also happy to set a 30-min call with procurement + legal to walk through.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_response_v1.docx (draft response)

Subject: Fwd: CloudWave MSA: redlines — need legal guidance on IP carveouts

Team — forwarding CloudWave’s redlines (below). Procurement wants explicit language and retention caps. Key commercial sensitivities: CloudWave will likely push for no training on any customer data (that could be a deal blocker). Pricing: if they require a full training opt-out and strict retention limits, we may need to price for increased cost of operation (no ability to leverage aggregated signals for proactive improvements).

Immediate asks: 
1) Kimberly — suggested clause snippets we can offer that balance their asks with our product roadmap.
2) Evelyn/Marcus — confirm whether the proposed telemetry carveout (aggregated, de-identified metrics only) is sufficient operationally; any telemetry items that would be necessary for us to retain for SLA/debug must be flagged.
3) Ben — I’ll coordinate the customer call once we have legal language to propose.

Quoted original (Lena):

> - CloudWave retains title to all customer outputs and artifacts produced by the service. No assignment to vendor.
> - No model training/fine-tuning on CloudWave data; any use of customer data for model improvement must be explicit opt-in and limited to anonymized telemetry.
> - Feedback license must be narrowly scoped: limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, solely for improving Redwood’s service for CloudWave, with options for opt-out.
> - Retention limits for logs and a clear deletion process on contract termination.

Ben

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: legal_ops <legal_ops@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: CloudWave MSA: redlines — suggested clause language

Team — reviewed CloudWave_MSA_redline_v3.docx. Below are draft clause suggestions and negotiation notes you can share with procurement. I attached a consolidated clause file (CW_redline_suggested_clauses.docx).

1) Outputs / Ownership (proposed):
"Customer Output Ownership: Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to any output, content, derivatives or artifacts that Customer or its End Users provide to or receive from the Service ("Customer Outputs"). Redwood Inference hereby assigns to Customer all of Redwood’s right, title and interest in any Customer Outputs generated specifically for Customer. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect and retain aggregated, de-identified telemetry (e.g., aggregate token counts, latency metrics, anonymized error classifications) solely for the purpose of monitoring, debugging, and improving the Service’s operational performance; such telemetry shall not include Customer Outputs or any Personal Data as defined in the Agreement."

Negotiation note: this accepts customer ownership while preserving a narrow telemetry carveout. Define "aggregated, de-identified" in the definitions section to reduce ambiguity.

2) Training / Model Use (proposed):
"No Training Without Opt-In: Redwood shall not use Customer Data, Customer Outputs, or Feedback to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any foundation or customer-facing model absent Customer’s prior written opt-in for such use. Customer may elect to provide a separate Training Opt-In, which shall be governed by a mutually agreed SOW and associated pricing. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry (as defined) for service improvement that does not constitute model training or re-training."

Negotiation note: replace the ambiguous term 'training' with 'train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any foundation or customer-facing model' to be explicit.

3) Feedback License (proposed):
"Limited Feedback License: To the extent Customer or End Users provide Feedback, Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable, worldwide license to use such Feedback solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Service for Customer and for aggregated product improvement efforts, provided that such use shall be limited to anonymized or aggregated forms and shall not include retraining of foundation models without Customer opt-in. Redwood shall not sublicense or transfer Feedback to third parties except as necessary to provide the Service and subject to confidentiality obligations."

4) Retention & Deletion: propose explicit retention periods (e.g., 90 days for request logs by default, unless customer elects a shorter window) and an API/process for deletion on request or termination. Add options for an extended retention mode for troubleshooting under an approved incident process.

5) Audit & Definition Clarifications: add definitions for "Anonymized", "Aggregated", and a short process for dispute resolution around alleged re-identification. Also recommend an SLA commitment around deletion timing (e.g., 30 days to purge customer data from operational caches after termination).

Next steps for customer outreach: Ben — send these two short clauses back to CloudWave procurement with an invitation to a 30-min legal sync. If procurement insists on a blanket ban on any use of telemetry or aggregated signals, escalate to pricing for the opt-out.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
Attachments: CW_redline_suggested_clauses.docx

- We need a proposed default retention period and the deletion workflow on termination.

If those items line up with our legal team’s appetite, we’re fine to schedule the 30-min call next week.

Lena Ortiz
